hero.label: The app for chronic back pain
hero.title: Take back what back pain took from you, one small step at a time.
hero.body: BackToHealth starts from your back, not from a generic program: a 5-minute assessment, guided exercises and a plan that slows down as soon as your pain goes up.
hero.phoneAlt: The app on a phone: the tree on the hill and today’s program

who.label: Sound familiar?
who.title: Your back has hurt for months. Maybe years.
who.body: You’ve heard it all and tried a lot. And you still hesitate before bending, lifting or driving for long. What you want is to do those things again without thinking about it.
who.fact: You are far from alone: about 9 times out of 10, back pain has no specific cause that can be identified.
who.forTitle: BackToHealth is made for you if
for: You’re an adult, and your back has hurt for months.
No serious cause explains it: this is non-specific low back pain.
You want to move forward at your own pace, without pressure.

water.label: Your day
water.title: A small plan each day. Not a mountain.
water.body: Reading, movement, meditation, walking: a few minutes each, and you do what you can. Every activity you finish waters your tree, so you can see your efforts add up.
water.end: Your tree never wilts. A missed day erases nothing: you pick up where you left off.

steps.label: Reading
steps.title: Understand, so you stop being afraid
steps.body: 23 five-minute lessons, written by our doctor, also trained in physiotherapy. When you understand your pain, you dare to move again.

steps.label: Movement
steps.title: Move without fear
steps.body: 5 to 15 minutes, 2 to 3 times a week. Exercises chosen for your back, which adjust to your pain.

steps.label: Meditation
steps.title: Breathe when pain weighs on you
steps.body: 3 to 30 minutes of mindfulness, so pain takes up less room in your day.

steps.label: Walking
steps.title: Get back into walking
steps.body: At your pace, with one goal a week. Yoga or cycling count too.

pain.label: Your pain decides
pain.title: Never more than your back accepts.
pain.body: The fear of making things worse is often what makes people stop. Here, you rate your pain after each set, and the program adjusts right away. Try it:
pain.easyBody: If your whole session goes like this: one more repetition next time.
pain.holdBody: You can keep going. Next time, same level.
pain.stopBody: Stop this exercise: it’s the right call. Next time, we start a little gentler. A 3-minute comfort moment is waiting for you.

screens.label: The app
screens.title: Simple, even on hard days.
screens.s1Body: A short plan. Nothing to catch up on.
screens.s3Body: You choose how much time you have.
screens.s4Body: What’s becoming possible again, in your own words.
screens.alt1: Today screen: a tree on a hill and a program of four activities
screens.alt2: Reading path screen: lessons joined by a trail across the hills
screens.alt3: Meditation screen on a night background: a choice of 5, 10 or 15 minutes
screens.alt4: Progress screen: gardening, carrying children and driving, each rated out of 10

pros.label: Physiotherapists and health professionals
pros.title: Your patients keep going between appointments. And after.
pros.body: Between two sessions, everything depends on what your patient does at home. BackToHealth guides them every day with your principles: screening, pain-dosed progression, education. Without replacing your assessment or your follow-up.
pros.ctaBody: We’re looking for clinicians to review the content and offer BackToHealth to their patients. Your feedback shapes the app.

cards.title: Screening comes first
cards.body: 8 red-flag questions. A positive answer points to a doctor or the ER, and the program doesn’t start.

cards.title: A progression you’ll recognise
cards.body: Above 3/10: stop, lower level. Session at 2/10 or less: one more repetition, up to 12, then the next level.

cards.title: In line with practice guidelines
cards.body: Exercise, pain education, mindfulness and walking, together, as recent guidelines recommend.

cards.title: Full transparency
cards.body: No diagnosis, no treatment, no published study yet. With people’s consent, we will measure what works.

team.label: The team
team.title: Three committed cofounders, in Montréal.
team.body: Medicine, software development and data science, brought together to help people live better with back pain.

people.name: Pierre-Henri Bao Heitz
people.title: Cofounder · Health sciences
people.bio: Physician, also trained in physiotherapy. He designed the BackToHealth care program with a scientific, methodical approach, based on recent research on chronic low back pain. He validates all of its content.

people.name: Adrien Moevus
people.title: Cofounder · App development
people.bio: Medical student and developer. He designed the architecture of the mobile app and built it, from the assessment to daily follow-up. He also wrote the guided meditations.

people.name: Antoine Moevus
people.title: Cofounder · Computing, AI and data
people.bio: PhD student in computer science at Université de Montréal (DIRO). An expert in artificial intelligence and data management, he set the technical direction of BackToHealth: data protection, outcome measurement and the use of AI.

items.q: Does it replace my doctor or physio?
items.a: No. The app complements your care. If something worries you, talk to a health professional.

items.q: What if it hurts too much, or I don’t feel like it?
items.a: Every activity has a “Not today” button. Flare-ups are part of the path: for 3 days, the plan eases off. Your tree and your progress are protected.

items.q: When does the app come out?
items.a: It’s in testing on iPhone and Android. Write to us to hear about the launch.
The price isn’t set yet. You’ll know clearly before launch.
French and English, following your phone. You can switch any time.
Protected, never sold. You can export or delete it any time. Research is optional and uses a code, never your name or email.

end.title: Your tree is waiting.
end.body: Write to us: we’ll let you know as soon as you can plant it.

footer.disclaimer: BackToHealth does not replace the advice of a health professional.

offer.label: The program
offer.title: 8 to 12 weeks to trust your back again. Then we stay.
offer.body: Four introductory programs teach you to understand your back, to move, to meditate and to walk. Then the app continues with you, for as long as you like.
offer.goalTitle: And after? You keep your tools.
offer.goalBody: Your exercises keep adapting, you meditate your way, you keep your walking rhythm. And you redo your tests to see how far you’ve come.

cards.body: 23 five-minute lessons to stop fearing your pain.
Progressive exercises that respect your pain, 2 to 3 times a week.
Learning to live with pain, rather than fighting it.
One goal a week, starting from what you already do.

meta.title: The program in detail · BackToHealth / Crescendos
meta.description: Exercises and dosing, 23 lessons, meditation and walking: what’s in BackToHealth, for patients and health professionals.

program.label: The program in detail
program.title: What BackToHealth contains, step by step.
program.lead: For the curious and for health professionals: the assessment, exercises, lessons, meditation and walking, as they are in the app.
program.status: Clinical content being validated by our doctor, also trained in physiotherapy. It may still change.
g3: 10 to 30 min, or 3 min of comfort
g4: 8 weeks, then at your own pace
eval: 8 red-flag questions. A positive answer points to a doctor or the ER, and the program doesn’t start.
4 movement tests (flexion, extension, right and left rotation), with the pain felt. They set the starting exercises and their level.
1 to 3 activities to get back to, rated from 0 to 10 (Patient-Specific Functional Scale).
The rhythm: a little every day, light and active days, or a few chosen days.
program.familiesTitle: The exercises, from easiest to most demanding
program.medDaily: Between sessions: finding that state for a few moments, 30 seconds to 2 minutes, effortlessly.
follow: The chosen activities are re-rated about every 2 weeks.
The movement tests are repeated about every 4 weeks, to compare.
Pain is tracked over time, with a weekly summary.
During a flare-up, 3 lighter days: no exercise, comfort moments and gentle walking.
Data can be exported at any time.
program.philoTitle: A toolbox, not a takeover of care
program.philoBody: BackToHealth gives the tools and the first steps. The program stands on its own; going further elsewhere (Pilates, meditation, clinic follow-up) is even better. The person stays in charge of their path.
program.glanceNote: These are the lengths of the introductory programs. The app then continues, with no time limit.
after: Exercises keep adapting, with new challenges when a level becomes easy.
Meditation continues with the practice built, from 10 to 30 minutes.
Walking keeps its rhythm, or rises to about 2 hours a week.
Lessons stay available, and the movement tests can be redone.
Going further elsewhere (Pilates, yoga, meditation, clinic follow-up) is encouraged.
program.exIdea: Moving without fear, guided by pain. The movement tests set the starting exercises: extension, flexion, rotation, trunk stabilisation, then strength (upper body, squat, lunge, hips). Up to 3/10, pain is acceptable: it doesn’t mean damage.
program.exProgress: 3 sets of 10 to 12 repetitions. Session at 2/10 or less: one more repetition; at 12, the next level. Above 3/10: stop, and one level down. When a family’s last level becomes easy, a harder exercise from another family is offered.
program.exExample: Glute bridge: 3 × 10, then 3 × 11, then 3 × 12, then Bird-dog at 3 × 10.
program.eduIdea: Understanding chronic pain to regain confidence: it’s real, but it doesn’t mean the back is damaged. Then lifestyle, pain management and acceptance and commitment.
program.eduProgress: One 5-minute lesson per active day, in order, with a question at each step.
program.medIdea: Living with pain rather than fighting it. Secular mindfulness, practised in sessions, then useful during the day.
program.medProgress: One guided session per practice, then free sessions with short reminders. 10 minutes in week 1, 15 after, up to 30 if wanted.
medThemes: The breath, and coming back when the mind wanders
The body scan, from head to feet
Kindness: talking to yourself as to a friend
What matters: stopping the struggle, thoughts as clouds, your values
program.walkIdea: Getting back into walking. A goal in minutes per week, never per day: a bad day can be made up later, or not at all.
program.walkProgress: It starts from what the person already walks (at least 15 minutes a week) and aims for about double in 8 weeks, from 45 to 125 minutes: about 10% more each week. Pain above 3/10: same goal. Two weeks in a row: walk as much as possible under 3/10, and start again from there.
program.walkExample: Starting at 30 minutes a week: 30, 33, 37, 40, 45, 49, 54, then 60 minutes.

eval.label: Your starting point
eval.title: A plan made for your back, not for everyone’s.
eval.body: Generic programs ignore where you are. In 5 minutes, BackToHealth looks at how your back moves and what you want to get back to. Your plan starts from there.

steps.title: Your safety first
steps.body: 8 questions spot the signs that call for a doctor. You start with confidence.

steps.title: Your back, as it is today
steps.body: 4 movements guided by video. You show how far you go and what you feel: your exercises are chosen from there.

steps.title: What matters to you
steps.body: Gardening, carrying your kids, driving: you choose 1 to 3 activities to get back to. They are what measures your progress.

eval.rangeAlt: The flexion position chosen with the slider

eval.tryLabel: Try it: this is the app’s real test
eval.resultUnset: Position {n} out of 10. Rate your pain to continue.

moves.label: Your exercises
moves.title: You always know exactly what to do.
moves.body: No more exercise sheets you can’t make sense of once you’re home. Every movement is shown in 3D, from the gentlest to the most demanding. You move up a level when your back is ready.

app.name: Flexion
app.intro: Standing, bend forward gently, as far as is comfortable.
app.watch: Watch the movement, then do it once, gently. Stop if it hurts too much.
app.rangeHint: Slide to the picture closest to your furthest position.
